name: Ion-wind carbon capture
subtitle: a fanless machine that quietly captures carbon dioxide

effects.effect: a sharp point at high voltage blows a breeze
molecules from a gas stick to a solid's surface

effect: a sharp point at high voltage blows a breeze
how: Machines that pull carbon dioxide out of the air must push enormous volumes of air past a sorbent, and their big fans are loud and costly to run, which keeps them out of cities. Here rows of needle points at high voltage blow a steady, silent breeze (electric wind) through thin sorbent sheets, which catch the carbon dioxide on their surfaces until they are warmed to release it for storage.
obstacle: Charged needles make a little ozone, which wears out the sorbents, so the points must be shaped to make almost none.
why: Silent, fanless air-moving lets carbon capture sit on city rooftops, next to the waste heat it needs.
real: Searches found EHD/ionic-wind fans (cooling, ventilation) and fanless wind-driven DAC contactors (Georgia Tech WEDAC) separately, but nothing pairing an ionic-wind fan with a DAC sorbent contactor.
